landscape.say: For homes: Security: Thicker safety film that holds broken glass together, slowing a break-in through garden apartment windows, back doors and first-floor sash. Glare Reduction: Film that softens low winter sun, snow glare and morning light off Lake Michigan so screens are readable and blinds can stay open. Energy-Saving: Films chosen to lower air conditioning load in summer and, with low-E options, keep more furnace heat indoors through a long Chicago winter. Home Tinting: Tinting for Chicago houses and condos, planned one elevation at a time.

landscape.label: Why Window Film Here
landscape.title: Why Window Film in Chicago Has to Work in Two Seasons
landscape.say: Most cities buy window film to fight sun. Chicago buyers have to think about both ends of the year. From June through September the city gets real heat and heavy humidity, and an east-facing high-rise unit near the lake or a south-facing bungalow front room can bake by midafternoon.

landscape.label: Local Know-How
landscape.title: Window Film, ComEd Bills and Chicago Heating Costs
landscape.say: Window film affects two utility bills here. In summer, solar heat that comes through glass is heat your air conditioner removes with ComEd electricity. In winter, heat that escapes through glass is heat your furnace or boiler replaces, usually on Peoples Gas in the city or Nicor in many suburbs.

landscape.say: Common questions: Is window film allowed in a Chicago high-rise condo? Usually, but many associations set rules on how film looks from outside, and some buildings require a certificate of insurance before work starts. How many years will interior window film hold up in Chicago? Good interior film usually stays in service for many years, often more than ten. Can window film be installed in a Chicago winter? Yes.

landscape.label: How It Works
landscape.title: How an install works

tiles.s: The quote form asks for your neighborhood
They check glass type, seals and frames
Each pane gets scraped and washed
Film needs time for trapped moisture to dry out

landscape.say: Here's how an install works. First, the quote form asks for your neighborhood, an approximate window count, the direction the glass faces and what is bothering you. Then, they check glass type, seals and frames, then hold samples on the actual windows so you can see tint, reflection and view. On install day, each pane gets scraped and washed. Finally, film needs time for trapped moisture to dry out.
